production_notes.no_quality_tier: This spec has no quality_tier dimension. All tasks are binary. Sealant type selection replaces QT as the cost/quality driver. No qt_rates or quality_tier_effects.
production_notes.no_access_modifier: Per KD-012 — caulking shares access equipment with adjacent painting spec. No separate FAC_EXT_ACCESS modifier. Production rates assume ground-level access already in place.
production_notes.joint_complexity_split: Two production rate tiers based on joint_complexity: simple_bead (100-150 LF/hr apply) and backer_rod (75-100 LF/hr apply). Split is driven by joint width threshold (3/8 inch).
production_notes.crew_assumption: 1-person crew for all caulking tasks. Caulking is a sequential one-person operation — gun, tool, move.

caulk_input_group.description: All LF-based tasks consume joint LF from direct estimator capture. Simple bead tasks use (IN_LF_CAULK_JOINT_TOTAL - IN_LF_CAULK_JOINT_BACKER_ROD). Backer rod tasks use IN_LF_CAULK_JOINT_BACKER_ROD. FIXED tasks are per-project allowances.

task_production_rates.name: Ground Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: LF/hr for laying drop cloth along base of wall below joint work zone. Caulking produces minimal debris — lightweight edge-only protection. ~9 sec per LF. Faster than full painting drop cloth setup because coverage is narrow (drip zone only, not full wall projection).

defect_tolerance.all: Drop cloth positioned below entire joint run. Secured against wind. No gaps in coverage under active work zone.

task_production_rates.name: Adjacent Surface Tape Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: LF/hr for applying painter's tape along both sides of joint on finished surfaces. Rate is per LF of joint (tape runs both sides = 2x tape LF consumed per 1 LF of joint). ~24 sec per LF of joint. UV-resistant exterior-grade tape. Not all joints require taping — conditional on finished adjacent surfaces.

defect_tolerance.all: Tape firmly pressed to substrate on both sides of joint. Clean, straight lines. No gaps or wrinkles. Tape edge aligned to intended sealant bead width.

task_production_rates.name: Material Staging
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fixed time per project for staging sealant tubes, caulk gun, utility knife, and backer rod (if applicable). Includes cutting tube tip at 45-degree angle, loading gun, and test bead on scrap. Verify sealant type matches specification. ~10 minutes for typical residential exterior.

defect_tolerance.all: Correct sealant type staged per specification. Tube tip cut to match joint width. Gun loaded and tested. Backer rod staged if joint_complexity = backer_rod.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Joint Surfaces
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: LF/hr for cleaning dust, debris, and construction dirt from joint cavity on new construction joints. NC scope = light prep only (compressed air, dry brush, rag wipe). ~18 sec per LF. No old caulk removal — joints are open and clean. Rate assumes ground-level access in place.

defect_tolerance.all: Joint sidewalls clean, dry, and free of dust. No standing moisture. No oil, grease, or construction adhesive residue. Both sidewall surfaces ready for sealant adhesion.

task_production_rates.name: Install Backer Rod
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: LF/hr for installing closed-cell foam backer rod into joints > 3/8 inch wide. Includes selecting correct rod diameter (joint width x 1.25), cutting to length, and pressing to consistent depth (1/4 inch below joint surface). ~20 sec per LF. Continuous installation — no gaps through corners.

defect_tolerance.all: Rod 25% larger than joint width for compression fit. Seated 1/4 inch below joint surface — not flush, not recessed > 1/2 inch. Continuous run — no gaps. Rod serves as bond-breaker preventing three-sided adhesion.

task_production_rates.name: Apply Sealant — Simple Bead Joints
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: LF/hr for gun-and-tool caulking on simple joints (no backer rod). Rate includes gunning continuous bead at consistent rate and immediately tooling to concave profile. Midpoint 125 LF/hr from research range 100-150. ~29 sec per LF. Tooling is integral — not a separate time adder.
task_production_rates.quantity_note: Engine uses (IN_LF_CAULK_JOINT_TOTAL - IN_LF_CAULK_JOINT_BACKER_ROD) for simple bead LF when both complexity types coexist on same project.

defect_tolerance.all: Continuous bead — no voids or skip areas. Concave profile with full substrate contact on both sidewalls. No sealant smear on adjacent face surfaces beyond tape line. Proper width:depth ratio maintained.

task_production_rates.name: Apply Sealant — Backer Rod Joints
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: LF/hr for sealant application over installed backer rod. Slower than simple bead due to wider joints, deeper fill, and precision depth control. Midpoint ~87 LF/hr from research range 75-100. ~41 sec per LF. Rate includes gunning continuous bead filling from rod surface to joint face and immediate tooling to concave profile.

defect_tolerance.all: Sealant fills from backer rod surface to face of joint. Concave profile. Full sidewall contact on both sides. No sealant forced past backer rod into cavity. Two-sided adhesion only — backer rod prevents bottom bond.

task_production_rates.name: Visual Joint Inspection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: LF/hr for walking all completed joints and visually inspecting for: continuous bead (no voids), proper concave profile, clean lines, correct sealant type. ~7 sec per LF. Fast pass — inspector walks along joint run checking for obvious defects. Flag joints needing touchup before sealant skins.

defect_tolerance.all: 100% visual inspection of all joints. No voids, no skip areas, no adhesive bridges across joint. Concave profile on every joint. Clean adjacent surfaces — no sealant smear.

task_production_rates.name: Spot Adhesion Verification
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: LF/hr for spot adhesion verification — light thumb-press test on representative joints (every 50-100 LF or one per elevation). Not a destructive pull test. Rate is high because only representative joints are tested, not every LF. ~6 sec per LF amortized. Time is dominated by walking between test points.

defect_tolerance.all: At least one test per elevation or per 100 LF. Sealant firmly bonded to both sidewalls on thumb press. Any pull-away indicates adhesive failure — flag for rework.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Masking Tape
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: LF/hr for pulling masking tape at 45-degree angle away from sealant bead while sealant is still wet/tacky. Rate per LF of joint (tape on both sides = 2x tape LF pulled per 1 LF of joint). ~18 sec per LF of joint. TIME-SENSITIVE — must remove before sealant skins over tape edge.

defect_tolerance.all: Clean sealant line after tape removal. No tearing of sealant bead. No tape residue on substrate. Tape removed before sealant skins.

task_production_rates.name: Site Cleanup & Protection Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fixed time per project for removing drop cloths, disposing of empty sealant tubes, backer rod offcuts, tape waste, and tube tips. Includes cleaning caulk gun nozzle. ~15 minutes for typical residential exterior. Bag waste for disposal — sealant tubes are not recyclable.

defect_tolerance.all: All protection materials removed. No sealant waste left on site. Drop cloths folded and stored. Caulk gun cleaned for next use.

factor_modifiers.name: Joint Complexity Factor
factor_modifiers.description: Drives task activation between simple_bead and backer_rod task variants rather than modifying rates. Simple bead tasks activate for narrow joints; backer rod tasks activate for wide joints (> 3/8 inch). This is a task selection factor, not a rate multiplier — each task variant has its own calibrated base rate.

simple_bead.notes: Standard joint — gun and tool, no backer rod. 100-150 LF/hr.

backer_rod.notes: Wide joint — backer rod install + sealant application. 75-100 LF/hr for apply, 150-200 LF/hr for rod install.

factor_modifiers.stacking_notes: Not a rate multiplier — controls which tasks are active. No stacking interaction with other modifiers.

quality_tier_effects.description: No quality tier dimension for this spec. Caulking quality is driven by sealant_type (material selection) and joint_complexity (labor/technique). Every caulk joint either meets the standard or fails — there is no economy/premium tier progression.
quality_tier_effects.round_configurations: See sop_modules.json — RC_CAULK_SIMPLE and RC_CAULK_BACKER_ROD control module/task activation based on joint_complexity.

polyurethane_cure_gate.blocks: All finish coat tasks in adjacent painting specs
polyurethane_cure_gate.production_impact: No direct rate impact — this is a scheduling delay between caulk completion and paint finish coats. Affects project duration, not labor hours.
polyurethane_cure_gate.notes: Water from paint causes flash cure and surface bubbling on uncured polyurethane. Absolute gate — no exceptions. Schedule caulking early in project to absorb cure time.

sequencing_rule.prerequisite: Substrate primer on adjacent surfaces applied before caulking
sequencing_rule.notes: Sealant adheres better to primed surfaces. Sequence: substrate primer -> caulk -> cure -> finish coats.

assumptions.value: All production rates assume ground-level work with access already in place
assumptions.note: Caulking shares access equipment with adjacent painting spec. No separate access modifier applied. If caulking at height without adjacent painting access, rates would need FAC_EXT_ACCESS adjustment — but this scenario is outside normal workflow.

assumptions.source: Field practice — caulking is a sequential one-person operation
assumptions.note: Doctrine does not specify caulking crew size. One person operates the caulk gun and tools the bead in a single pass. Helper tasks (protection, cleanup) are also single-person. A second person would not meaningfully increase throughput on the same joint.

assumptions.value: 500 LF/hr for visual inspection, 600 LF/hr for spot adhesion check
assumptions.source: Researcher analysis — derived from walk-along inspection pace
assumptions.note: No doctrine rate for caulk joint inspection. 500 LF/hr (~7 sec/LF) is a brisk walking inspection. 600 LF/hr for adhesion check is faster because only representative joints are tested. Both rates are estimates pending field calibration.

assumptions.value: 150 LF/hr masking rate is per LF of joint — includes taping both sides
assumptions.note: Tape runs both sides of joint (2x tape LF per 1 LF joint). The 150 LF/hr rate accounts for this — it is the joint production rate, not the tape production rate. Same logic applies to tape removal at 200 LF/hr.

assumptions.source: Estimation based on typical residential exterior scope
assumptions.note: Caulking cleanup is minimal — collect empty tubes, backer rod offcuts, tape waste, clean gun. 15 minutes is appropriate for typical residential. Larger projects may need proportionally more time — field calibration recommended.

risks.description: Tape masking percentage is uncertain — materials.json flags 50% estimate for joints requiring tape. Actual percentage varies by project. If all joints require taping, masking and tape removal time doubles vs. estimate.
risks.mitigation: Estimator override for tape coverage percentage. Rate per LF is correct — the quantity (how many LF get taped) is the variable.

risks.description: Backer rod installation rate assumes consistent joint widths. Mixed-width joints requiring rod size changes mid-run will slow installation.
risks.mitigation: Use rate_range_low (150 LF/hr) for projects with highly variable joint widths. Rate_range_high (200 LF/hr) for uniform joints.

risks.description: Apply rates assume ground-level access. Caulking on upper elevations (ladder/scaffold) without adjacent painting spec access setup would need FAC_EXT_ACCESS modifier not included in this spec.
risks.mitigation: Per KD-012, this scenario should not occur — caulking is always scheduled during painting access setup. If it does occur, apply FAC_EXT_ACCESS from the painting spec's factor table.

validation_plan.description: Field-time 50 LF of simple bead caulking (gun + tool). Target: 20-30 minutes (100-150 LF/hr). Record joint width and substrate type.
Field-time 50 LF of backer rod installation + sealant application. Target: 26-40 minutes combined (75-100 LF/hr apply + 150-200 LF/hr rod). Record joint width and rod sizing.
validation_plan.expected_outcome: Confirm 87 LF/hr baseline for TSK_CAULK_APPLY_BACKER and 175 LF/hr for TSK_CAULK_BACKER_ROD.

validation_plan.description: Field-time tape masking and removal on 50 LF of joints. Record both setup and teardown times separately.
validation_plan.expected_outcome: Confirm 150 LF/hr for TSK_CAULK_MASK_ADJACENT and 200 LF/hr for TSK_CAULK_TAPE_REMOVE.

validation_plan.description: Field-time joint cleaning on NC joints (50 LF). Record substrate type and debris level.
validation_plan.expected_outcome: Confirm 200 LF/hr for TSK_CAULK_JOINT_CLEAN on clean NC joints.
